activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
story:
Blake went to the garden center with Dad. She picked out tiny carrot seeds. "I will plant a big number of seeds," she said. Dad laughed. "Ten is a big number for you."

Blake put the seeds in dirt. She made two pots. She watered one pot every day. She forgot the other pot. The watered pot grew little green tops. The dry pot grew nothing at all. "Hey!" said Blake. "This pot has no water. That is why!" She gave the dry pot a big drink.

Soon both pots had green tops. The tops grew tall. Blake pulled one carrot up. It was small and young. She washed it and took a bite. "Mmm," she said. "The next one is for you, Dad."

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
story:
Matteo wanted his red socks. He could not find them. He looked under the bed. He looked in the toy box. No red socks.

Mom sat down next to him. "You wore them yesterday," she said. "Yesterday is the day before today." Matteo put his finger on his chin. Yesterday he played in the snow. His socks got wet. Mom washed them after that.

Matteo ran to the drying rack. There they were! His red socks hung up, still warm from the radiator. "I know why they are here," he said. "They got wet yesterday. You washed them yesterday. They dry now. Later they will be dry all done." Mom smiled and clapped her hands.

"Can I wear them tomorrow?" Matteo asked. "Yes," said Mom. "Tomorrow comes after you sleep." Matteo got into bed. He pulled the blanket up to his chin. "Sleep now, socks," he whispered. "See you tomorrow." He closed his eyes. Mom turned off the light.

activity: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
knowledge_domain: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
story:
Harper went to the pharmacy with Dad. She saw a boy at the sink near the door. He was washing his hands. He sang a song while he washed.

"Dad, why does he sing?" Harper asked.

"Watch and see," said Dad.

Harper watched. The boy sang the whole song. Then he pointed at a sign. The sign said twenty seconds. "Soap needs time," the boy said. "A quick rinse does not work."

Harper wanted to try. Dad helped her reach the sink. She put soap on her hands. She sang her song, "Twinkle, twinkle, little star." She sang it all the way through. Then she rinsed the soap off.

"Dad, my hands are clean!" she said. "The song made me slow down. Slow soap wins!"

"Slow soap wins," said Dad, laughing. "Now let's go get your medicine."

At home, Harper washed before lunch. She washed after the toilet too. She sang every time. Her hands were clean. The soap had time to work.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Gabriel ran to Grandpa's house on his little bike. The sun was hot, so he parked the bike under the tree. "I want to paint," said Gabriel. Grandpa gave him a brush and some paint. There was red paint. There was blue paint. There was yellow paint. But there was no green paint. Gabriel wanted to paint the green grass. Grandpa said, "Try things and see."

Gabriel dipped his brush in yellow. He painted a yellow sun. Then he dipped the same brush in blue. He made a dot on the paper. "Oh!" said Gabriel. The dot was green! Yellow and blue made green. He painted the grass with his new green. "Yellow and blue make green," he said. Grandpa smiled.

Then Gabriel chewed his apple while his painting dried. Grandpa hung it up on the wall. And there, at the bottom, Gabriel found one more surprise. A tiny green dot was on his thumb. "Grandpa, my hand is green too!" Grandpa laughed. "Let's wash it in the sink, and then we can paint some more."

activity: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
knowledge_domain: to name the primary colours and mix two of them to make a new colour
story:
Eliana went to the art gallery with her dad. A big monkey statue sat by the door. It looked thirsty, so Eliana pretended to give it her juice. "Here, monkey," she said.

Inside, Eliana saw paintings everywhere. One room was all red, blue, and yellow. "Those are the big colours," said a lady with paint on her hands. Eliana touched the wet yellow wall. Then she touched the blue wall next to it. Her fingers made green!

She stared at her hand. "Yellow and blue," she said slowly. "They cook up green!" She tried again on paper. Red plus yellow made orange, like a sunset. Red plus blue made purple, like a plum.

Eliana ran back to the monkey statue. She held up her purple fingers. "Look what I made!" she said. "Blue and red cook purple!" The monkey did not move, but Eliana was sure it winked.

activity: to count a group of up to ten objects and say which of two groups has more
knowledge_domain: counting, comparing amounts, and shapes
fact: When you count a group of things, the last number you say tells how many there are. You get the same answer no matter which one you count first.
story:
At school, Miss Kim put out two plates of crackers. "Which plate has more?" she asked. Ethan wanted to answer, but he did not know.

He watched the crackers on the blue plate. He made a line with his finger and counted. "One, two, three, four, five." The last number was five. So there were five crackers.

Then he counted again. This time he started at the other end. "One, two, three, four, five." Five again! Ethan smiled. The last number was the same. It did not matter where he began.

Then he counted the red plate. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven." Seven crackers!

"Miss Kim!" said Ethan. "The red plate has more. It has seven. Seven is more than five."

Miss Kim clapped her hands. "Well done, Ethan."

Ethan picked up one naughty cracker that had rolled off the plate. He put it back in line, counted once more, and said, "Still seven!"

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Hannah sat on the train with her teddy. The train went fast. Rain ran down the window in little lines. "Look, teddy, the rain is dancing," said Hannah.

Then Hannah wanted her yellow cup. "Where is my cup, Mama?" Mama looked in the big bag. She looked under the seat. No cup. "Your cup is at home," said Mama. "We can't get it till we go back." Hannah frowned. At home, the cup sat on the table. But the table was far, far away now. The train could not turn around for one little cup. "Silly train," said Hannah. Papa laughed. "Silly cup," he said. "It is home drinking all the juice by itself." Hannah giggled. She thought her cup might be lonely.

Mama held up a paper cup from the snack cart. "This cup can be yellow too," said Mama. She put a yellow sticker on it, a little sun with a smile. "New cup, new friend," said Hannah. She gave teddy a sip. Teddy got a dot of juice on his nose. Outside, the rain stopped. Hannah watched the sun come out. "The rain went home too," she said. "Just like my cup." Papa kissed her head. "Everything goes home," he said. The train went on. Hannah waved at the sun.

activity: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
knowledge_domain: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
story:
Tonight was candle night at Grandma's house. Eleanor put on her red dress. It was Diwali, the festival of lights.

Eleanor wanted to hold a candle too. Mama said, "First we light the big lamp. One lamp, two lamps, three little lamps." Eleanor counted with her. The flames jumped up, warm and bright. They smelled like sweet flowers. Then Mama gave Eleanor one small candle. It was messy with wax on her fingers. "Why does my candle go out?" Eleanor asked. Grandma smiled. "You tipped it. The wax ran out." Eleanor held it very still, straight up like a tree. The flame stayed on!

Grandma touched Eleanor's cheek. "Good holding, little one." Eleanor watched her flame dance. "My candle is still on," she said.

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
story:
Sophie and Grandma went to the garden. Sophie had a little pig toy in her pocket. The pig had a round pink nose. Sophie patted his nose. Then she planted three seeds.

Every day Sophie came back. She wanted to see her seeds. She dug in the dirt to look. But the seeds did not grow. Sophie felt sad. "My seeds are broken," she said. Grandma held her hand. "Seeds need to sleep in the dark," said Grandma. "Let them stay under the dirt."

So Sophie stopped digging. She gave the seeds water instead. The sun came up each day. It was not late when she watered. Then one morning, Sophie saw a green sprout. "It grew because I let it sleep!" she said. Sophie turned her face up to the sun and smiled. The little pig watched too.

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
Elias stood on a small stool. He was at the big community kitchen. He wanted to bake bread for his mama and papa. He mixed flour and water and a little honey. He made a soft, round ball of dough.

He put the dough in a pan. He slid the pan into the oven. Then he waited. He waited a long time. He peeked in. The bread was still pale and flat. A tiny mouse ran along the wall. "Look, little mouse," Elias whispered. "My bread will not puff up."

Then he saw it. The oven was not hot. He had not turned the knob. No heat meant no baking. Elias turned the knob. A soft warmth filled the oven. He waited again. This time the bread grew round and gold. The kitchen smelled warm and sweet.

"Is it ready?" asked Mama. Elias tapped the bread. It sounded hollow inside. "It is ready!" he said. Papa tore off a piece and smiled. Elias cut a thick slice for himself. "Hot ovens make bread bake," he whispered to the mouse. "I turned it on, so now we eat."

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
story:
Sara wanted to win a game at school. The game was called the five senses game. But she did not know all the answers yet.

Mama had an idea. "Let's play at home," she said. Mama put an orange on the table. Sara looked at it with her eyes. She smelled it with her nose. She touched the bumpy skin with her hands. Mama cut it open. Sara took a small bite with her mouth. Then Mama clapped, and Sara heard the sound with her ears.

"Now count them," said Mama. Sara held up her fingers, one at a time. "Eyes, nose, hands, mouth, ears." That was five. Then Mama shook a toy snake with a bell inside. Sara held it up high and listened. "I hear the bell with my ears," she said. Mama smiled. "You know all five now," she said. "Let's play one more time." Sara put the orange back on the table and began again.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Isla ran to the big slide. It was tall and shiny in the sun. "Too hot!" she said. Her hands let go fast. The sun made the slide hot, so it burned a little.

She went to the small slide instead. It sat in the shade of a tree. She touched it with one finger. This slide was cool. Down she went, slow at first. Then she went again, and she went fast. "Whee!" she shouted. A boy laughed. "You go fast when you stand up less," he teased. Isla sat down flat. She slid so fast her hair flew up.

After the slides, she was thirsty. Mom had a water bottle. The water was cold. Isla drank it all up. "The sun makes things hot," she said. "The shade makes things cold." Mom gave her a towel to sit on, and Isla lay in the shade. The towel was soft and cool, and soon she was not sleepy at all, wide awake and ready for the swings.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story:
Samuel wanted his blue coat. It had a circle patch on the pocket. The coat rack was full of coats.

Samuel looked and looked. He saw a coat with squares. He saw one with triangles. Where was his circle?

Then he heard his teacher. "Time to go outside!" The room got loud. Samuel needed his coat fast.

He touched each coat. Squares had four sides. They felt pointy. His circle patch felt round and smooth. No points!

Then he felt something round. It rolled a little under his hand. It was the circle patch!

"Found it!" said Samuel. He put on the coat.

His teacher laughed. "How did you know?"

"The circle is round," said Samuel. "It rolled on my hand!"

The room was quiet now. Everyone was outside. Samuel ran out the door. "Wait for me!"

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
story:
Olivia wanted to paint at the little table. But her brother Sam was already there. He had all the cups of paint. All six cups!

"I want blue," said Olivia.

"Blue is mine," said Sam.

Olivia frowned. She looked at the big sheet of paper. It was cloudy and grey, because Sam used grey on everything.

"How many cups do you have?" Olivia asked.

Sam counted. "One, two, three, four, five, six."

"That is not fair," said Olivia. "Six for you and zero for me."

Sam looked at her face. He pushed three cups across the table. "One, two, three," he said. "Now it is fair."

Olivia took the blue cup. She painted a big blue cat. Sam painted a red sun.

Then the brush fell on the floor. "I can fix that," said Sam. He picked it up and wiped it clean.

"Now you go first," said Olivia. "Then it is my turn."

They took turns, back and forth, back and forth. The picture got bigger and bigger.

Mama came to look. "What a lovely cat and sun," she said. "Who made this?"

"We both did," said Sam. "We shared the paint."

"And we took turns," said Olivia. She smiled and gave Sam the blue cup. "Now blue is yours."

activity: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
knowledge_domain: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
story:
Logan ran into the baby store. "Baby sister is coming soon!" he said. Mom held his hand. "We need a cozy blanket," she said. Logan saw a red one. He touched it. It was soft like his teddy bear. "This one!" he said.

Then Logan saw tiny shoes. They were so small. He put his shoe next to one. His shoe was much bigger. "Baby feet are little," said Logan. "So the shoes are little too!" Mom laughed. "That's right, Logan."

Logan picked a cozy blue hat. It fit on his hand like a mitten. He followed Mom to the strollers. Then a small surprise! Dad was hiding by the cribs. "I bought a crib already," said Dad. Logan clapped his hands. "Now baby sister can sleep!" he said. They all went home with the red blanket.

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
story:
Mila sat at the little table. She had red paint and yellow paint. She wanted to paint a big apple.

First she painted the apple red. Then she wanted a yellow leaf on top. She put her brush in the yellow paint. She touched the red apple with it. Oh no. The yellow spot turned orange.

"Why did it turn orange?" Mila asked. She looked at her brush. The brush still had wet red paint on it. The wet paints mixed on the paper.

So she washed her brush in the water cup. She dried it on a paper towel. Now the brush was clean. She got fresh yellow paint. She sent the clean brush across the paper. The yellow stayed yellow!

She painted a little yellow leaf. It sat on top of her red apple. Her teacher smiled. "What a lovely apple," she said.

Mila held it up to the window. "Clean brush, yellow leaf," she said softly.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Ellie ran onto the green field. Her team wore white shirts. Daddy sat on the bench by the shed door. "Kick the ball, Ellie!" he called.

The ball rolled to Ellie. She stopped it with her hands. She picked it up and hugged it. The coach blew the whistle. "No hands, Ellie. Feet only. Hands mean the other team gets the ball." Ellie put the ball down. The other team took it, and they ran far away.

Ellie felt like crying. Daddy waved from the bench. "Try again," he said.

The ball came back. This time Ellie used her foot. She tapped it and tapped it. Then she kicked it hard. The ball went into the net! Ellie's team did win the game. Daddy lifted her up high. "You used your feet," he said. Ellie laughed and hugged her white shirt close.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Brooks ran to the big red slide. He wanted to play house, but he had no baby. Then he saw a stuffed bunny near the sand. "I can be your dad," Brooks said to the bunny.

He found a box for a bed. One, two, three leaves went on top. "Soft bed for you," he said. The bunny kept falling out. Brooks stopped and looked. The box was on the hill. The hill was slanted. That was why the bunny fell.

He thought hard. Then he moved the box to flat ground. "Flat ground, no falls," he said. The bunny stayed in the bed. It stayed and stayed.

A girl named Mia came over. "Can I be the doctor?" she asked. "Yes," said Brooks. "My baby needs a check." Mia tapped the bunny's tummy one, two, three times. "All better," she said. Brooks hugged the bunny tight. "Time for bed, little one."

activity: to count a group of up to ten objects and say which of two groups has more
knowledge_domain: counting, comparing amounts, and shapes
fact: When you count a group of things, the last number you say tells how many there are. You get the same answer no matter which one you count first.
story:
Clara went to the community centre with her dad. There was a play room with a tall shelf of toys. On the table sat two plates of cookies.

"May I have cookies?" Clara asked. Miss Amy smiled. "You may have the plate with more," she said.

Clara looked at the plates. She could not tell which had more. So she counted the red plate. "One, two, three, four, five," she said. Then she counted the blue plate. "One, two, three, four," she said. Four came last, so four was less than five.

Then Clara counted the red plate again. This time she started from the other end. "One, two, three, four, five," she said. Five again! She counted once more from the middle. It was still five.

"It is five every time," Clara said. "I get the same answer."

She took the red plate. She ate one cookie, slowly and happily. Outside, a car went past the window, and the big bell began to ring. It was song time.

"Come on," said Miss Amy. Clara ran to the circle, holding her last warm cookie.

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
story:
Lena sat in the big waiting room chair. Her feet did not touch the floor. She held a card with her name on it. She was going to the dentist for the very first time.

A lady called, "Lena, come in." Lena sat in a soft chair that tipped back. The dentist said, "I will count your teeth." Lena shut her mouth tight. The dentist could not see anything.

Then Lena saw a little mirror. She wanted to see it too. She opened her mouth very wide. "Ah," she said. Now the dentist could see every tooth. He counted one, two, three, all the way to twenty.

"Open wide, and I can see," said Lena. The dentist smiled and gave her a sticker. It was a shiny tooth.

activity: learning to swim at the local pool
knowledge_domain: learning to swim at the local pool
story:
Raphael went to the little pool by the lake. The water was cool on his toes. Dad helped him tie the strings of his swim shorts. "Now I will swim!" said Raphael.

Raphael put his face in the water. He came up fast. "Ow! My nose has water in it," he said. He tried again. Water went up his nose again. "Why does the water go in?" he asked. Dad said, "Try one thing. Blow out like this. Puff, puff."

Raphael put his face down. He blew out. Bubbles came out of his nose. He came up smiling. "The water stayed out!" he said. "My nose was too busy blowing bubbles!"

Dad laughed. "Good swimmer!" Raphael blew more bubbles. "Look, Dad! Bubble nose!" Then he splashed Dad with a big kick.

activity: getting through an evening power cut at home
knowledge_domain: getting through an evening power cut at home
story:
The lights went out. Matthew stood in the backyard with Dad. The porch light was off too.

"Is it dark everywhere?" Matthew asked.

They went inside. Dad found a flashlight. Dad clicked it. No light came out.

"Old batteries," said Dad. He put in two new batteries. He clicked again. Now a bright beam shone on the wall.

"New batteries make it work!" said Matthew. He clicked it on and off, on and off.

They sat on the step. Matthew shone the light on his toy bus. The bus looked yellow in the beam.

"How long do the lights stay off?" Matthew asked.

"Till the men fix the wires," said Dad.

Matthew held the flashlight on his bus. The little wheels gleamed. "Bus, we can see you," he said.

activity: to spread butter on toast and pour milk into a cup without spilling
knowledge_domain: to spread butter on toast and pour milk into a cup without spilling
story:
Aubrey woke up hungry. She wanted toast with butter and a cup of milk. "I can do it myself," she said.

Dad put warm toast on her plate. Aubrey dug her knife into the cold butter. The butter made a big lump and tore the toast. She tried again on the warm part. The butter went soft there and slid on like paint. "Warm toast makes butter melt," she said. She spread it all the way to the corners.

Next came the milk. She lifted the carton up high and tipped it fast. Milk splashed out onto the table. The dog ran in and began to bark at the puddle. He stepped in it and left a stinky wet foot print on the floor.

Aubrey got a cloth and wiped the table. Dad wiped the dog's paw. Then she tried again. This time she held the carton close to the cup. She tipped it just a little bit. The milk slid in slow and quiet. Not one drop fell. "You have to pour slow," Aubrey told the dog. The dog wagged his tail and licked up her toast crumbs.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Zoey sat on the blue mat at daycare. Miss Rita held up a book. "This morning I went to the library," she said. "You can borrow books there and take them home."

Miss Rita opened the front cover. She turned page one, page two, page three. Zoey counted along. "One, two, three!"

The book was about a sweet little bear who patted every dog he met. Pat, pat, pat. Zoey laughed.

"I want to keep this book forever," said Zoey.

Miss Rita smiled. "But we must bring it back. Then other kids can read it too."

Zoey thought hard. Then she patted the book, soft and gentle, like the bear patted the dogs.

"Bye bye, book," she said. "New kids are coming to read you."

She turned the pages one more time, front to back, all by herself. "One, two, three. The end!"

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
story:
Eliana sat in the car seat. She was going to the dentist for the first time. "I wonder what a dentist does," she said.

Mama parked the car. They went in together. The dentist had a big chair. It went up and up, like a rocket. Eliana laughed.

The dentist looked in Eliana's mouth. "I see little bits of dirt on your teeth," she said. "We will wash them off." She used a tiny brush. It tickled. Then she put some paste on it. The paste tasted like bubblegum! "It tastes sweet," Eliana said. "Teeth paste can taste good?"

The dentist rinsed with water. The water washed the dirt away. Eliana looked in a little mirror. Her teeth were shiny and white. "The water made them clean," she said. "That is why they shine!"

In the car, Eliana was hungry. Mama had an apple in her bag. Eliana took a big bite. "My teeth feel so smooth," she said. She smiled all the way home.

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Edouard sat on his bed with a new book. It was about a blue bird in a garden. He got it at the library with Mama. He had his very own card now, with his name on it.

"I want to keep this book forever," Edouard said.

Mama sat down next to him. "The book has a due day," she said. "We take it back so other kids can read it too."

Edouard held the book tight. "But I love the blue bird."

"You can draw the bird," said Mama. "Then your picture stays."

Edouard found his crayons. He drew the blue bird in the garden. Then he put the book in his bag.

"Tomorrow we take it back," he said. "Then a new book comes home with me."

"Good plan," said Mama. She tucked him in.

"Night night, blue bird," said Edouard.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
story:
Eliana stood by the gate. The playground looked very big. She wanted a friend, but everyone was new. A boy ran past her. A girl climbed the slide. Nobody knew Eliana's name yet.

Then Eliana saw something on her shirt. Her mom had pinned a tag there. It said ELIANA in red letters. A girl with a dog backpack came close. She looked at the tag. "Your name is Eliana!" she said. "My tag says Mia." Mia pointed at her own red letters.

"You read my tag!" said Eliana. "That is how you know my name!" Mia laughed. "The tags tell us," she said. "Clever tags." Then the sky turned stormy, so they ran inside together. "Sit by me," said Mia. Eliana sat down fast.

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
story:
Brooks sat in his cozy car seat. He held his little toy plane. Today he would meet the dentist. He did not know what a dentist would do.

"Will it hurt?" he asked.

"Let's find out together," said Mom. "Hold my hand in the big chair."

At the dentist, Brooks sat in a chair that went up and down. The dentist smiled. She held a tiny mirror. "Open wide," she said. "I will count your teeth." She counted out loud. "One, two, three." Brooks kept his lips shut at first. Then he opened them a tiny bit.

"Look, twenty teeth!" said the dentist. "Now they are clean and shiny."

Brooks jumped down from the chair. He waved his toy plane high.

"Teeth get counted because they get clean," he told Mom. "And it did not hurt one bit."

The dentist gave him a sticker shaped like a star.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Lillian wanted her teddy bear. He was a gift from the toy shop. But the hall was dark. She could not see. She felt scared. Her tummy felt tight.

Then Daddy turned on the light. The hall was bright now. Lillian looked around. There was no monster. There was only a coat on a hook. The scary dark was gone. Her scared feeling got small. She smiled a big, happy smile.

"Dark made me scared," said Lillian. "Light helps!"

She walked down the hall. She found her teddy under a chair. Daddy clapped for her. Lillian felt so excited. She hugged teddy tight.

Then she heard a loud crash. Oh no! The cat had knocked down a cup. Lillian ran to look. The cat looked sorry. Lillian giggled.

"Kitty made the crash," she said. "I heard it first!"

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
story:
Parker wanted to steer the rocket. The rocket was a big cardboard box. Mia was holding the wheel.

Parker grabbed the wheel. "My turn!" he said. Mia pulled it back. The rocket wobbled. The rocket nearly tipped over. "The rocket is wobbly because we both hold the wheel," said Parker.

Mia found a sand timer. "You watch the sand," she said. "When the sand goes down, it is your turn." Parker watched the sand. It went drip, drip, down. Then the sand was all gone. Mia let go of the wheel.

Parker steered the rocket all alone. They flew past stars. Outside it was very dark and shiny. They landed at the moon park. The moon park had a bumpy slide.

"Your turn now," said Parker. He held out the wheel to Mia. Mia smiled. They took turns until the moon came up over the playroom window. "Next stop, the star park!" said Mia.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
story:
It was Sophia's birthday! She was three years old today. The bowling alley was loud and bright. The balls went rumble, rumble down the floor.

"Happy birthday, Sophia!" said Grandma.

Sophia picked a big blue ball. She pushed it hard. The ball went crooked. It rolled into the gutter. No pins fell down.

"You went too fast," said Dad. "The pins need you to wait. Then the machine sets them up again."

Dad showed her. He pointed his feet straight. He rolled slow. Crash! All the pins fell down!

Sophia tried again. She pointed her feet. She rolled slow. Crash! Eight pins fell!

"Too fast, they fall down wrong. Slow, they fall down right!" said Sophia. Everyone clapped.

Then came the cake. There were three real candles. Sophia made a wish and blew them all out.

"Do not forget the ice cream," said Grandma.

Sophia ate her ice cream with a little pink spoon. "Best birthday ever!" she said. Grandma gave her one more big hug.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Parker found the old paint cups at school. He wanted to paint green grass. But there was no green cup. There was red. There was blue. There was yellow. No green at all.

Parker dipped his brush in blue. He made a blue stripe. He made a yellow stripe under it. Then he kept painting. The stripes touched. He rubbed his brush back and forth.

"Look!" said Parker. "The blue and yellow made green!"

His teacher came to see. "You made green all by yourself," she said. Parker painted big green grass. He painted a green frog too.

At play time, Parker went down the slide. He saw green grass at the bottom. "Same green as my paint!" he said.

His friend Mia slid down next. "Show me green paint later?" she asked.

"Yes," said Parker. "Blue and yellow. That is how."

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story: Hailey wanted to make a house for her pet cat. She got paper and tape. First she taped a circle on top. The circle was round like a ball. It rolled off. "Oh no," said Hailey. "The circle rolls. It will not stay." She tried a square. The square was flat and had four sides that were the same. It stayed on, but the rain could not run off in her picture. Then she tried a triangle. The triangle had three sides and a pointy top. "This looks like a real roof," she said. Mom helped her pull the tape tight. The triangle roof stayed on. The cat jumped in. "The circle rolled because it was round," Hailey said. "The triangle stays because it is pointy." Mom smiled. "Nice work, Hailey." The cat curled up under the pointy roof. It was not scary at all. It was cozy.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Natale put on her red shirt. It was her team shirt for soccer. Dad walked with her to the backyard, where the coach was waiting.

Natalie wanted to pass the ball to her friend Sam. She kicked it with her toe. The ball jumped up high. It went over Sam's head. It hit the fence with a knock. Then it rolled under a bush.

"Why did the ball go up so high?" Natalie asked.

The coach rolled the ball back. Natalie looked at her foot. She tried again. This time she kicked the ball with the inside of her foot. The ball stayed low. It rolled right to Sam.

"Sam caught it!" said Natalie. "The inside of my foot keeps the ball down."

Sam kicked it back. Natalie trapped it with her foot. Then she passed it again, low and slow.

A little feather blew across the grass. The ball was quiet now, not bumpy. Natalie stepped on the crunchy leaves by the fence. They made a fun sound.

"Good pass, Natalie," said Dad from his chair. He clapped his hands.

Natalie smiled. She held the ball under her arm. "One more pass," she said. "Watch me, Dad."

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Mila wanted tea for her toy cat. She looked in the playroom. She could not find her small teapot. "Where is it?" she asked. She found it under the cat's long tail.

Mila poured from the big teapot. The tea went all over the table. "Oh no," she said. She poured from the small teapot. The tea fit in the tiny cup. "The big one holds too much," she said. "The small one is just right."

The tea was pretend hot. She blew on it. Slow, slow, slow. Then she pretended to sip. "Is it hot or cold now?" she asked. "Cold," she said. "Slow blowing makes it cold."

The cat drank fast. Mila drank slow. "Just right," said Mila. She held the cup up to the cat's soft ear.

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
story:
Elijah sat by the rink wall. Papa sat on one side. His friend Mia sat on the other. The big game was starting.

The glass in front of Elijah turned white and foggy. He could not see the players. He rubbed the glass with his mitten. A clear spot opened up. He could see the ice again. Then his warm breath touched the glass. The fog came back. Elijah rubbed it again, slow and slow. The spot opened up again. He kept the spot clear while he watched.

"The players are so fast," said Mia. Elijah watched and waited. The skates went zip, zip, zip. The air smelled cold and fresh. Then the puck slid toward the net. Nobody moved. Elijah held his breath.

The puck went in! "We got a goal!" Elijah shouted. Papa clapped his hands. Papa leaned down and gave Elijah a kiss on the head. Mia laughed and clapped too.

Elijah looked at the glass. His fog spot was still there. He pointed with one finger. "The glass gets foggy because I breathe on it," he said. He took a big breath and blew. Fog bloomed like a little white cloud. Then he rubbed it clean one more time and watched the players skate on.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story:
Isaac sat at the dinner table. He had ten little peas on his plate. He wanted to eat them one by one.

"One, two, three," said Isaac. He pushed the peas with his spoon. Then he stopped. He did not know what came next. He made a small noise. "Stuck," he said.

Daddy was washing the big pot at the sink. He came over and sat down. "Want to sing it?" said Daddy. Daddy sang the counting song from play group. Isaac knew that song! He sang too. "Four, five, six, seven." The song went on. "Eight, nine, ten!" Now he knew them all.

Isaac looked at his plate. The song helped him remember. "The song says the numbers," he said. Daddy nodded.

Isaac ate the peas. He counted each one. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten." All gone! Daddy gave him a warm hug.

"Bedtime comes early tonight," said Daddy. "But first, one more song."

"Ten little peas went crunch, crunch, crunch," sang Isaac.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Margot sat on her big bed. She had a library book about a stinky skunk. She loved that skunk. She wanted to keep him forever.

"One skunk, two skunks, three stinky skunks," she counted on the pages. She read the words out loud. "Skunk. Bed. Hat." The words told her things! She turned the pages one by one, front to back.

Then Mama came in. "Library day is today," said Mama. "The book goes back so other kids can read it too."

"No! My skunk stays with me," said Margot. She held the book tight.

"But then no one else gets the skunk," said Mama. "And you can borrow a new book."

Margot thought. She took her crayon and drew her own skunk. Then she let the book sink down into the book bag.

"Bye, skunk," she said. "Hello, new book."

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Noah put on his red shirt. It was his team shirt for soccer. He ran out to the backyard to practice.

Dad rolled the ball to him. Noah caught it with his hands. He held it tight and ran.

"No, no," said Dad with a smile. "In soccer, we use our feet. Not our hands. Try a little kick."

Noah put the ball down. He tapped it with his shoe. The ball went straight to Dad. Noah tapped it again. The ball rolled under the big tree, near the wooden horse on the swing set.

"Oops," said Noah. He ran to get the ball. "I guess I kicked it too hard," he said.

Dad nodded. "A soft kick goes a short way. A big kick goes far."

The sun was going down. They did not want to be late for dinner. Noah gave the ball one more soft kick. It rolled right to Dad's feet.

"Team practice done," said Dad.

Noah held up his hands. "See? No hands!"

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Gabriel wanted his red ball. It rolled under the big chair. He could not reach it.

Gabriel felt angry. His face got hot. He stomped his foot. "Bad chair!" he said.

Mama came in. She was a kind woman. "Take a big breath," she said. "Then try again."

Gabriel took a big breath. His face did not feel so hot. He got down on his tummy. He reached far. Still no ball.

"I need a stick," Gabriel said. He found a wooden spoon. He pushed it under the chair. The ball rolled out. It rolled right to his hand.

"I did it!" Gabriel said. He jumped up and down. He felt so excited.

Then the doorbell rang. It made a loud noise. Gabriel felt scared. He held Mama's leg.

"It is just Grandpa," said Mama. Grandpa came in. He had a small dog. The dog licked Gabriel's face.

Gabriel laughed. He felt happy now. He threw the red ball. The dog ran after it.

Gabriel clapped. "Big breath first, then throw," he said. He took a big breath. He threw the ball again, far, far across the room.
